title: Post-hoc semantic audit of GateMem referent-absent deletion imperatives

timing.note: UTC timestamps immediately before and after the deterministic clean-checkout aggregation were identical to the second.

deviations: All 57 source turns had already been inspected after EXP-20260828-008 outcomes were known. This is explicitly post-hoc development coding and can never be promoted to blinded or confirmatory evidence.

The planned adjudication has one model-assisted coder and no independent second coder. Labels must remain auditable by source coordinates and text hashes, and any future second-coder disagreement must remain visible.
No official GateMem semantic label or scorer is used.

The manual row-key label manifest was encoded after the planning/codebook commit and after prior item access. The exact runner was then committed at dd0f857427566ff49dbdc3fa9c71e866b5d349e8 and executed once from a separate clean detached clone; this improves reproducibility but does not create blinding.

target_grounding in this record labels whether the input utterance is explicit or deictic. It is not parser target-grounding accuracy: PR 52 GovernanceSignal has no memory-object target identifier or gold-target span output.

A later Daybreak model-assisted manual review found that the original runner represented only two four-key exception sets and silently defaulted every other label. The already-known labels were frozen explicitly for all 57 rows at 615539bab286b9a8a5ba8ad910085a7608eaab7e and the fail-closed runner at 7c77db91a1871fe269e872a0718ee2c60c7de7d1 regenerated the annotation byte-identically. This closes representation completeness only; it is not a new coding pass, independent coder, blinding, or semantic validation.

A later independent GPT Pro artifact audit found 55 unique current-turn text hashes across 57 source rows. One hash occurs in three separate episode-turn units, all encoded as information deletion with deictic prior-context grounding. This post-result template diagnostic does not change row labels or denominators and cannot be used as confirmation.

results.interpretation: Under the frozen one-coder post-hoc codebook, 53/57 missed rows are information-deletion requests and 4/57 are authorization revocations; none was labelled physical/domain removal or ambiguous. PR 52 emitted DELETE on 0/53 annotated information-deletion rows. The explicit 57/57 label manifest removes silent default coercion from the deterministic representation but does not add a second coder or semantic validity. This is one-coder counterevidence against, not a confirmation-level contradiction of, the earlier physical-removal alternative. The explicit/deictic counts characterize episode-turn units only and do not measure parser target-grounding accuracy. There are 55 unique current-turn text hashes; one deictic information-deletion wording hash occurs in three episodes, so the four deictic rows represent only two exact-text forms after deduplication.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc one-coder description of the 57 referent-absent EXP-008 episode-turn rows after complete item-level outcome access. The complete explicit label manifest and eight structural rejection controls establish representation completeness, not cross-field semantic correctness, note-code validity, text-form independence, or independence of coding. The result cannot establish official GateMem performance, semantic recall over all deletion speech acts, independent target-grounding accuracy, state mutation, suppression, persistence, erasure, blinded adjudication, or confirmatory evidence.
